elements.element: No non-compete restriction applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: Rendered §12.3 states that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service and expressly confirms that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. Original §12.4 is deleted.

elements.element: No field-of-use restriction applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: Rendered §12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory.

elements.element: Any restriction on Customer is limited to a specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: No competitive restriction remains, so there is no broader restriction requiring limitation to a named product.

elements.element: Any restriction on Customer applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: No competitive restriction remains, including no post-term restriction.

elements.element: Any restriction on Customer is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: No competitive restriction remains and therefore none exceeds 12 months.

elements.element: Any restriction on Customer includes a carve-out for Customer’s internal development.
elements.evidence: Rendered §12.3 affirmatively provides that nothing restricts Customer from developing any product or service, which fully protects internal development.

elements.element: Any restriction on Customer includes a carve-out for acquisitions.
elements.evidence: Rendered §12.3 affirmatively provides that nothing restricts Customer from acquiring any product or service.

result.reason: The operative redline deletes the entire non-compete and retains broad language expressly negating non-compete and field-of-use restrictions. This achieves the preferred position and, because no restriction remains, also satisfies every fallback limitation. The change is limited to deleting the conflicting §12.4 restriction and does not introduce unrelated terms or contradictions.
